newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yul Brynner's "Magnificent Seven" gear auctioned.
newsitem.headline: Yul Brynner's "Magnificent Seven" gear auctioned.

text.p: The cowboy hat worn by the late film star Yul Brynner in the film "The Magnificent Seven" was sold for $14,600 at an auction in Paris, organisers said on Tuesday.

Among other Brynner memorabilia auctioned on Monday night were Brynner's Colt revolver, sold for $12,800 to an anonymous buyer, and his black boots which fetched $7,000, a spokesman for auctioneers Tajan said.
An unnamed Texas collector bought the black, French-made hat.

A note hastily scribbled by director Cecil B. de Mille, making Brynner the pharoah in the epic "The Ten Commandments", sold for $4,400. The silk costumes the actor wore in "The King and I", for which he won an Oscar in 1957, went for $2,880,
Other items included pipes and cigarette cases that belonged to Brynner, who died of lung cancer in 1985.

The auction, which brought in a total of $842,000, also included guitars, paintings, sculptures, books, cameras and antique furniture collected by Brynner at his 16th century Criqueboeuf country manor in Normandy, western France.
